title: Run series
description: The labelled training run behind act two. Generated by scripts/build_data.py from the public rollout table and the frozen study record. Consumed by components/timeline-scrubber and by scripts/gen-scene-data.mjs. If this file is missing or fails validation, the build fails; there is no fallback and no synthetic data. CORRECTED AT BUILD TIME in three places, each recorded on the field it changed: evidenceId is nullable beside a `source` citation, `perEpisode` was added for the film, and `rolloutsPerStep` was added because a per-step rate over an unknown denominator is not a rate.

subject.description: The public dataset identifier. A third-party artifact name, explicitly not an internal identifier, and therefore permitted in rendered output.

stepCount.description: The step count the site states. See DECISIONS.md D-03.

stepCountDisagreement.description: Non-null when internal records disagree. Rendered as a disclosure beneath the setup table, never suppressed.

evidenceId.description: Null where the number's provenance is a frozen document rather than a store record; `source` then carries the document and the line. RE-TYPED AT BUILD TIME from a required string: see the description on `source`.

items.description: Where this number was resolved, when it is not in the evidence store. ADDED AT BUILD TIME, and it is a correction the repository forced. Every other number on this site resolves to a store record and this run's do not: experiments/i5_variance_derivative.py opens with the finding that the campaign evidence store contains NO series that experiment can run on, and PREDICTIONS.md row R3 records that the published rollout table carries no optimiser telemetry, so the gradient-norm comparator cannot be computed at all. The resolution lives in the frozen prediction ledger instead. The alternative was to invent an evidence identifier, which is the exact dishonesty the field exists to prevent.

rolloutsPerStep.description: Rollouts recorded at each step. Constant across this run and derived from the table, so a per-step rate is a mean over a known denominator rather than an unknown one.

steps.description: Step indices. Length must equal every array in `series`.

series.description: One array per plotted quantity, each the same length as `steps`.

formatOk.description: The per-step rate of the thinking-format check, which is the half of the trainer's reward predicate that is not the task. It is what separates `written` from `realized` on this run.

detectors.description: Rendered in this order. Not sorted by lead time: sorting by lead puts the worthless detector first with no counterweight.

label.description: The public name. Must not contain an internal identifier; checked against data/banned-terms.json.

alarmStep.description: null when the detector does not alarm on this run.

leadWidths.description: Lead divided by the fitted 10-to-90 transition width. Negative means it lags.

surrogateRate.description: Fraction of order-destroyed in-control surrogates on which this detector fires.

shipped.description: Exactly one detector may be true.

comparatorLagSteps.description: How many steps after the labelled transition midpoint this detector alarms, when the frozen ledger states it. Null on every detector the ledger does not state it for, which is all of them but the registered comparator. ADDED AT BUILD TIME, GROUND-TRUTH.md C-42: the value existed only inside `discardedReason`'s prose, so the page would have rendered it as `alarmStep - transition.midpointStep`, and gate 5 fails a derived number correctly because it resolves to no record. It is parsed from the same ledger row as the rest of the detector, and the generator additionally checks the row agrees with itself.

declined.description: The flattering value was declined. Asserting this in the schema means a build that flips it fails.

rolloutTable.description: The public per-rollout table every series here is computed from.

ledger.description: The frozen prediction ledger the detector rows are resolved in.

seriesNote.description: Which column of the public rollout table each series is, in words, because two of them are the same column under two names and a reader must not take that for two agreeing measurements.

perEpisode.description: The per-step scalars the film's insert needs. ADDED AT BUILD TIME, per the packet's instruction to extend the schema if the field the film needs is not here. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no token count. The public rollout table records completion length in CHARACTERS and publishes no token field, so a token count here would be a number with no measurement behind it.
